revealWordProblem.title: Apply: Car Sales
revealWordProblem.text:
A car dealership's sales for one month are shown in the monthly sales report. The owner now needs to order 50 cars from the factory.
Question: Based on the sales shown, how many of each type of car do you recommend the owner order?
revealWordProblem.imageAlt: A monthly sales report bar graph out of 100 cars sold: 8 hybrid, 18 all-electric, and 74 gas-powered.
revealWordProblem.sampleAnswer: Out of 100 cars sold, 8 were hybrid, 18 were all-electric, and 74 were gas-powered, so those counts are already percents: 8%, 18%, and 74%. Apply each percent to the 50-car order: 8% of 50 = 4 hybrids, 18% of 50 = 9 all-electric, and 74% of 50 = 37 gas-powered. That accounts for all 50 cars (4 + 9 + 37 = 50), so I recommend ordering 4, 9, and 37.

vocabulary.definition: A rate compares different units; a unit rate compares a quantity to 1 unit.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Una tasa compara unidades diferentes; una tasa unitaria compara una cantidad con 1 unidad.
vocabulary.visual: 180 miles in 3 hours = 60 miles per 1 hour.
vocabulary.cloze: A rate compares different units; a ___ ___ compares a quantity to exactly 1 unit.

examples.why: It gives the amount for one unit.
A rate, but not yet per one.

vocabulary.definition: A ratio comparing two amounts with different units, like miles per hour.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Una razón que compara dos cantidades con unidades distintas, como millas por hora.
vocabulary.cloze: A ratio that compares two quantities with different units is a ___.

examples.why: Two different units compared.
A single measurement, not a comparison.

vocabulary.definition: A rate for just 1 of something, like cost for 1 item.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Una tasa para solo 1 de algo, como el precio de 1 artículo.
vocabulary.cloze: A rate that tells the cost or amount for one unit is a ___.

examples.why: It gives the amount for exactly one unit.
That is a rate for 3 units, not a unit rate.

vocabulary.definition: For each one. Example: 5 dollars per book.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Por cada uno. Ejemplo: 5 dólares por libro.
vocabulary.visual: 60 miles per hour means 60 miles for every 1 hour
vocabulary.cloze: The word that means 'for each one' is ___.

examples.text: $5 per book meaning $5 for each book
examples.why: It means “for each one”.
That is a total for three, not each.

vocabulary.definition: A way to compare two amounts, like 3 to 2.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Una manera de comparar dos cantidades, como 3 a 2.
vocabulary.cloze: A comparison of two quantities is a ___.

examples.why: Two quantities compared.
Nothing to compare it against.

vocabulary.definition: A unit rate that gives the cost of exactly 1 item, like $0.60 per game.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Una tasa unitaria que da el costo de exactamente 1 artículo, como $0.60 por juego.
vocabulary.cloze: A unit rate that tells the cost of one item is the ___ ___.

examples.why: It gives the cost of exactly one item.
It is a unit rate, but it is not a cost.

vocabulary.definition: The choice that costs less for each item.
vocabulary.definitionEs: La opción que cuesta menos por cada artículo.
vocabulary.visual: Pack A: $0.50 per pencil vs Pack B: $0.40 per pencil — Pack B is the better buy
vocabulary.cloze: The option with the lower unit rate, costing less per item, is the ___.

examples.why: The lower cost per item wins.
More is not cheaper per token.

vocabulary.definition: Splitting a total into equal groups.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Repartir un total en grupos iguales.
vocabulary.cloze: To find a unit rate, I ___ the price by the number of units.

examples.why: Splitting a total into equal parts.
That grows the total instead of sharing it.

vocabulary.definition: A percent is a ratio that compares a number to 100, so every percent answers the question “how many out of 100?”
vocabulary.definitionEs: Un porcentaje es una razón que compara un número con 100, así que todo porcentaje responde “¿cuántos de cada 100?”
vocabulary.cloze: A ratio comparing a number to 100 is a ___.

examples.text: 65 shaded squares out of a 100-square grid is 65%
examples.why: It compares the part to a whole of exactly 100.
The whole is not 100, so the count is not the percent.

vocabulary.definition: Three equivalent ways to name the same part of a whole.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Tres maneras equivalentes de nombrar la misma parte de un todo.
vocabulary.cloze: Three equivalent ways to name the same part of a whole are ___, ___ and ___.

examples.why: All three name the same amount of the same whole.
0.2 is a different amount, so the set is not equivalent.

vocabulary.definition: A way to compare a number to 100, shown with the % sign.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Una manera de comparar un número con 100, con el signo %.
vocabulary.cloze: A ratio that compares a number to 100, written with a % sign, is a ___.

examples.text: 9 out of 100 students walk to school → 9%
examples.why: The comparison is already out of 100.
That is 90%, not 9% — both terms must be scaled to 100.

vocabulary.term: Percents Greater Than 100% and Less Than 1%
vocabulary.termEs: Porcentajes mayores que 100% y menores que 1%
vocabulary.definition: Percents can describe amounts greater than one whole or smaller than one hundredth of a whole.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Los porcentajes pueden describir cantidades mayores que un entero o menores que una centésima de un entero.

vocabulary.definition: A number with a dot, like 0.5, that shows a part less than one.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Un número con un punto, como 0.5, que muestra una parte menor que uno.
vocabulary.cloze: A number that uses a point to show parts of a whole is a ___.

examples.why: The percent divided by 100 gives the decimal.
Multiplying by a plain 35 makes the answer 100 times too big.

vocabulary.definition: A percent bigger than 100%, more than the whole thing.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Un porcentaje mayor que 100%, más que todo el entero.
vocabulary.cloze: A percent that represents more than one whole, like 150%, is ___.

examples.why: 150% is more than one whole (100%).
75% is less than one whole.

conceptIntro.heading: The Big Ideas — Lessons 3.2 · 4.1 · 4.2
conceptIntro.intro: Here is the one thing to remember from each lesson, plus a quick guided example. If one of these feels shaky, that lesson is right above this one in the menu — you can open it any time.
conceptIntro.keyIdea: 3.2: To find a unit rate, divide the total cost by the number of items. A unit rate that gives a cost is called a unit price, and the lower unit price is the better buy. • 4.1: A percent is a ratio comparing a number to 100. The whole is always 100%, so a percent above 100 means MORE than one whole. • 4.2: To turn a fraction into a percent, build an equivalent fraction with a denominator of 100: ask “what do I multiply the denominator by to get 100?” and multiply the numerator by that same number. The new numerator is the percent.

iDo.title: The Big Ideas (one per lesson)
lines: Lesson 3.2 — Understand Rates and Unit Rates: To find a unit rate, divide the total cost by the number of items. A unit rate that gives a cost is called a unit price, and the lower unit price is the better buy.
Lesson 4.1 — Understand Percent: A percent is a ratio comparing a number to 100. The whole is always 100%, so a percent above 100 means MORE than one whole.

Lesson 4.2 — Relate Fractions, Decimals, and Percentages: To turn a fraction into a percent, build an equivalent fraction with a denominator of 100: ask “what do I multiply the denominator by to get 100?” and multiply the numerator by that same number. The new numerator is the percent.
linesEs: Lección 3.2 — Comprender las tasas y las tasas unitarias: Para hallar una tasa unitaria, divide el costo total entre el número de artículos. Una tasa unitaria que da un costo se llama precio unitario, y el precio unitario más bajo es la mejor compra.
Lección 4.1 — Comprender el porcentaje: Un porcentaje es una razón que compara un número con 100. El entero siempre es 100%, así que un porcentaje mayor que 100 significa más de un entero.

Lección 4.2 — Relacionar fracciones, decimales y porcentajes: Para convertir una fracción en porcentaje, forma una fracción equivalente con denominador 100: pregúntate «¿por cuánto multiplico el denominador para llegar a 100?» y multiplica el numerador por ese mismo número. El nuevo numerador es el porcentaje.

discourse.sentenceFrame: I multiplied the top and bottom of ___ by ___ to get ___/100, so the percent is ___%.

approaching.stem: (Lesson 3.2) A booth charges $4.50 for 9 games. What is the unit rate?
choiceFeedback: Double-check your division: $4.50 ÷ 9 — is it $0.45 or $0.50?
Divide the cost by the number of games: $4.50 ÷ 9, not some other operation.
That's the total cost for all 9 games, not the cost for one game.
hints: You know the total cost ($4.50) and the total games (9). A unit rate tells the cost of just ONE game.
To find a unit rate, divide the total cost by the number of games so the second quantity becomes 1.
Set up the division: $4.50 ÷ 9. Think of $4.50 as 450 cents if that makes the division easier.
approaching.stemEs: Un puesto cobra $4.50 por 9 juegos. ¿Cuál es la tasa por unidad?
hintsEs: Conoces el costo total ($4.50) y el total de juegos (9). Una tasa unitaria dice el costo de UN solo juego.
Para hallar una tasa unitaria, divide el costo total entre el número de juegos para que la segunda cantidad sea 1.
Plantea la división: $4.50 ÷ 9. Piensa en $4.50 como 450 centavos si eso te facilita la división.

approaching.stem: (Lesson 3.2) A car travels 180 miles using 6 gallons of gas. What is the unit rate in miles per gallon?
choiceFeedback: That's the number of gallons — you need to divide 180 by 6, not use 6 as the answer.
Check your division: 180 ÷ 6 — is it 30 or 36?
That's the total miles — divide 180 by 6 to find miles for one gallon.
hints: Notice the units in the question: miles PER gallon. That tells you miles go on top and gallons on the bottom.
Divide the total miles by the total gallons so you get the miles for just 1 gallon.
Start the division: 180 ÷ 6. Think: 6 × what number lands on 180?
approaching.stemEs: Un carro recorre 180 millas usando 6 galones de gasolina. ¿Cuál es la tasa por unidad en millas por galón?
hintsEs: Fíjate en las unidades de la pregunta: millas POR galón. Eso te dice que las millas van arriba y los galones abajo.
Divide el total de millas entre el total de galones para obtener las millas de 1 solo galón.
Empieza la división: 180 ÷ 6. Piensa: 6 × ¿qué número da 180?

approaching.stem: (Lesson 4.1) What does the word percent mean?
approaching.explanation: Percent means per hundred, which is why every percent can be written as a fraction with a denominator of 100.
choiceFeedback: Per ten would be a tenth, not a percent.
Per thousand is a different comparison entirely.
"Part" does not say how big the whole is; a percent always compares to 100.
hints: Look at the second half of the word: cent.
A century is 100 years; a cent is 1/100 of a dollar.
Percent = per 100.
approaching.explanationEs: Por ciento significa por cada cien, y por eso todo porcentaje se puede escribir como una fracción con denominador 100.
hintsEs: Mira la segunda parte de la palabra: ciento.
Un siglo son 100 años; un centavo es 1/100 de dólar.
Por ciento = por cada 100.

approaching.stem: (Lesson 4.1) 3 out of every 10 students walk to school. What percent is that?
approaching.explanation: Multiply both terms of the ratio by 10 to compare to 100: 3 out of 10 becomes 30 out of 100, or 30%.
choiceFeedback: 3 out of 100 would be 3%, but the ratio here is out of 10.
10 is the second term of the original ratio, not the percent.
That adds the two numbers instead of scaling the ratio.
hints: A percent compares to 100, so rewrite the ratio out of 100.
What do you multiply 10 by to get 100?
Multiply BOTH terms by that same number.
approaching.stemEs: 3 de cada 10 estudiantes caminan a la escuela. ¿Qué porcentaje es eso?
approaching.explanationEs: Multiplica los dos términos de la razón por 10 para compararla con 100: 3 de 10 se convierte en 30 de 100, o sea 30%.
hintsEs: Un porcentaje compara con 100, así que reescribe la razón sobre 100.
¿Por cuánto multiplicas 10 para obtener 100?
Multiplica AMBOS términos por ese mismo número.

choiceFeedback: Try again: 5 × 20 = 100, so multiply the top by 20 as well.
Build an equivalent fraction with denominator 100 — multiply the top and bottom by the same number.
hints: Percent means out of 100. What do you multiply the denominator 5 by to get 100?
5 × 20 = 100, so multiply the numerator by that same 20 to build the equivalent fraction.
3 × 20 = 60, so 3/5 = 60/100. A fraction out of 100 IS the percent.
hintsEs: Porcentaje significa de cada 100. ¿Por cuánto multiplicas el denominador 5 para llegar a 100?
5 × 20 = 100, así que multiplica el numerador por ese mismo 20 para formar la fracción equivalente.
3 × 20 = 60, entonces 3/5 = 60/100. Una fracción de cada 100 ES el porcentaje.

choiceFeedback: Scale 7/20 up to a denominator of 100 first.
Double-check: 20 × 5 = 100, so the top must be multiplied by 5 too.
hints: The denominator 20 is friendly: 20 × 5 = 100, and percents are always 'out of 100'.
Make an equivalent fraction with denominator 100 by multiplying top AND bottom by the same number.
Multiply 7/20 by 5/5: the bottom becomes 100. Whatever the top becomes is your percent.
hintsEs: El denominador 20 es amigable: 20 × 5 = 100, y los porcentajes siempre son 'de cada 100'.
Forma una fracción equivalente con denominador 100 multiplicando arriba Y abajo por el mismo número.
Multiplica 7/20 por 5/5: la parte de abajo se vuelve 100. Lo que quede arriba es tu porcentaje.

onLevel.stem: (Lesson 3.2) Token packs: Pack A is 20 tokens for $5.00, Pack B is 35 tokens for $7.00, and Pack C is 50 tokens for $12.50. Which pack is the best deal per token?
onLevel.explanation: Pack B has a unit rate of $0.20 per token, which is the lowest cost per token.
choiceFeedback: Compare the cost per token, not the total price or the total number of tokens. Divide each pack's price by its tokens and compare those results.
A bigger pack is not automatically cheaper for each token. Work out price ÷ tokens for every pack before deciding.
Compare the unit rates: $0.25, $0.20, and $0.25. Are all three the same?
hints: The 'best deal' is the pack where ONE token costs the least — not the pack with the most tokens.
Line up the three unit rates you found in the table and look for the smallest cost per token.
Compare $0.25, $0.20, and $0.25 per token. Which of those is the smallest amount of money?
onLevel.stemEs: Paquetes de fichas: el Paquete A trae 20 fichas por $5.00, el B trae 35 por $7.00 y el C trae 50 por $12.50. ¿Cuál paquete es la mejor oferta por ficha?
onLevel.explanationEs: El paquete B tiene una tasa por unidad de $0.20 por ficha, que es el menor costo por ficha.
hintsEs: La 'mejor oferta' es el paquete donde UNA ficha cuesta menos — no el paquete con más fichas.
Alinea las tres tasas unitarias que hallaste en la tabla y busca el menor costo por ficha.
Compara $0.25, $0.20 y $0.25 por ficha. ¿Cuál de esos es la menor cantidad de dinero?

onLevel.stem: (Lesson 3.2) Runner A completes 4 laps in 12 minutes. Runner B completes 5 laps in 14 minutes. Who runs more laps per minute?
onLevel.explanation: Runner A: 4÷12 ≈ 0.33 laps/min. Runner B: 5÷14 ≈ 0.36 laps/min. Runner B runs slightly more laps per minute.
choiceFeedback: You found 4 ÷ 12, but compare: is 0.33 laps per minute more or less than 0.36?
Divide each runner's laps by their minutes. You should get two different rates.
You have the laps and the minutes for both runners — that's enough to find and compare their rates.
hints: Each runner has laps and minutes. 'More laps per minute' means you need each runner's laps-per-minute rate first.
Divide laps by minutes for BOTH runners, then compare the two decimals — bigger decimal means faster.
Start with Runner A: 4 ÷ 12 ≈ 0.33 laps per minute. Now find Runner B's rate with 5 ÷ 14 and compare.
onLevel.stemEs: El corredor A completa 4 vueltas en 12 minutos. El corredor B completa 5 vueltas en 14 minutos. ¿Quién da más vueltas por minuto?
onLevel.explanationEs: Corredor A: 4 ÷ 12 ≈ 0.33 vueltas/min. Corredor B: 5 ÷ 14 ≈ 0.36 vueltas/min. El corredor B da un poco más de vueltas por minuto.
hintsEs: Cada corredor tiene vueltas y minutos. 'Más vueltas por minuto' significa que primero necesitas la tasa de vueltas por minuto de cada uno.
Divide vueltas entre minutos para AMBOS corredores y luego compara los dos decimales: mayor decimal significa más rápido.
Empieza con el Corredor A: 4 ÷ 12 ≈ 0.33 vueltas por minuto. Ahora halla la tasa del Corredor B con 5 ÷ 14 y compara.

onLevel.stem: (Lesson 4.1) The orange kitten weighs 1.5 times as much as the gray kitten. What percent of the gray kitten's weight is that?
onLevel.explanation: The gray kitten is the whole, or 100%. One and a half wholes is 100% + 50% = 150%.
choiceFeedback: 1.5% is a tiny sliver — but the orange kitten is heavier.
15% would be a small fraction of the gray kitten, not more than all of it.
50% is only half the gray kitten's weight.
hints: Which kitten is the whole?
One whole is 100%. What is half a whole?
Add the whole and the half.
onLevel.stemEs: El gatito anaranjado pesa 1.5 veces lo que pesa el gatito gris. ¿Qué porcentaje del peso del gatito gris es eso?
onLevel.explanationEs: El gatito gris es el entero, o 100%. Un entero y medio es 100% + 50% = 150%.
hintsEs: ¿Cuál gatito es el entero?
Un entero es 100%. ¿Cuánto es medio entero?
Suma el entero y la mitad.

onLevel.title: (Lesson 4.1) Find the error

workedExample.label: Setup
workedExample.work: A player scored 150% of the weekly goal of 200 points.
workedExample.workEs: Un jugador logró el 150 % de la meta semanal de 200 puntos.

workedExample.label: Step 3
workedExample.workEs: El jugador superó la meta de 200 puntos.

onLevel.correctWork: Step 2 reads the percent as if it were the points themselves. A percent is a comparison, not an amount: 150% of 200 points is 1.5 × 200 = 300 points.
onLevel.explanation: Step 3 even contradicts Step 2 — 150 points would fall short of a 200-point goal. A percent always needs a whole to be a percent OF.
hints: Steps 1 and 3 are both right — check Step 2.
150% of what?
onLevel.explanationEs: El Paso 3 hasta contradice al Paso 2 — 150 puntos no alcanzarían una meta de 200 puntos. Un porcentaje siempre necesita un entero DEL cual ser porcentaje.
hintsEs: Los Pasos 1 y 3 son correctos — revisa el Paso 2.
¿150% de qué?

onLevel.stem: (Lesson 4.2) A game shows your score as 7/8 complete. What percent is that?
onLevel.explanation: 8 does not scale to 100 by a whole number, so divide: 7 ÷ 8 = 0.875, and 0.875 × 100 = 87.5%. That is 87.5 out of 100.
choiceFeedback: Convert the fraction to a decimal first.
8 will not scale to 100 evenly — divide 7 by 8, then multiply by 100.
88% is the rounded version, but this score converts exactly. Divide 7 by 8 and keep every decimal place — the percent is not a whole number.
hints: Try the out-of-100 move first: is there a whole number you can multiply 8 by to get exactly 100?
There isn't (8 × 12 = 96, 8 × 13 = 104), so use the backup method: divide the numerator by the denominator.
7 ÷ 8 = 0.875, which is 87.5/100 — slide the decimal two places right to read the percent.
onLevel.stemEs: Un juego muestra tu puntaje como 7/8 completado. ¿Qué porcentaje es eso?
onLevel.explanationEs: 8 no escala a 100 con un número entero, así que divide: 7 ÷ 8 = 0.875, y 0.875 × 100 = 87.5%. Eso es 87.5 de cada 100.
hintsEs: Prueba primero el paso de cada 100: ¿hay un número entero por el que puedas multiplicar 8 para llegar exactamente a 100?
No lo hay (8 × 12 = 96, 8 × 13 = 104), así que usa el método de respaldo: divide el numerador entre el denominador.
7 ÷ 8 = 0.875, que es 87.5/100; desliza el punto dos lugares a la derecha para leer el porcentaje.

onLevel.title: (Lesson 4.2) Spot the Common Mistake

workedExample.label: Divide the bottom by the top
workedExample.labelEs: Divide el de abajo entre el de arriba

onLevel.correctWork: The student divided in the wrong order. To turn a fraction into a decimal, divide the TOP by the bottom: 5 ÷ 8 = 0.625, then × 100 → 62.5%. So 5/8 = 0.625 = 62.5%. (A check: 5/8 is less than 1, so the percent must be under 100%, never 160%.)
hints: Is 5/8 more or less than one whole? Then can its percent be over 100%?
8 will not scale to 100 evenly, so divide the numerator by the denominator: 5 ÷ 8 = 0.625, which is 62.5/100 → 62.5%.
onLevel.explanation: The fraction bar means numerator ÷ denominator, so this division is upside down. It should be 5 ÷ 8 = 0.625, and 0.625 × 100 = 62.5%. A quick check catches it: 5/8 is less than one whole, so its percent must be under 100% — 160% was impossible.
onLevel.explanationEs: La barra de fracción significa numerador ÷ denominador, así que esta división está al revés. Debe ser 5 ÷ 8 = 0.625, y 0.625 × 100 = 62.5%. Una comprobación rápida lo detecta: 5/8 es menor que un entero, así que su por ciento tiene que ser menor que 100%; 160% era imposible.
onLevel.correctWorkEs: El estudiante dividió en el orden equivocado. Para convertir una fracción en decimal, divide el de ARRIBA entre el de abajo: 5 ÷ 8 = 0.625, luego × 100 → 62.5%. Así que 5/8 = 0.625 = 62.5%. (Una comprobación: 5/8 es menor que 1, así que el porcentaje debe estar por debajo de 100%, nunca 160%.)
hintsEs: ¿5/8 es más o menos que un entero? Entonces, ¿puede su porcentaje pasar de 100%?
8 no se escala a 100 de forma exacta, así que divide el numerador entre el denominador: 5 ÷ 8 = 0.625, que es 62.5/100 → 62.5%.

onLevel.title: Fix our table's thinking

workedExample.label: The problem
workedExample.work: (Lesson 3.2) Token packs: Pack A is 20 tokens for $5.00, Pack B is 35 tokens for $7.00, and Pack C is 50 tokens for $12.50. Which pack is the best deal per token?
workedExample.workEs: Paquetes de fichas: el Paquete A trae 20 fichas por $5.00, el B trae 35 por $7.00 y el C trae 50 por $12.50. ¿Cuál paquete es la mejor oferta por ficha?

workedExample.label: A classmate at our table answered
workedExample.labelEs: Un compañero de nuestra mesa respondió

practice.commonMistake: A common mistake in Relate Fractions, Decimals, and Percents is treating the numerator and denominator as the percent's digits — turning 3/5 into "35%" by just reading the 3 and the 5. Percent means out of 100, so the fix is to build an equivalent fraction with denominator 100: 5 × 20 = 100, so multiply the top by 20 too — 3/5 = 60/100 = 60%. A second version of this mistake is scaling only ONE part of the fraction (writing 3/5 = 3/100 or 60/5). Whatever you multiply the denominator by, you must multiply the numerator by the same number. When a denominator will not reach 100 evenly (8, 3, 7), divide the numerator by the denominator instead and then multiply by 100.

connect.scenario: A store has a clearance sale: 'Everything 3/5 off!' Your friend says that means 35% off. Another friend says it's 60% off. The original price of a game is $40.
connect.promptQuestion: Who is correct, and how much would the game cost on sale?
connect.prompt: The friend who said ___% is correct because 3/5 = ___ = ___%. The sale price is $___.

check.stem: '3/5 off' means 3 of the 5 equal parts come off the price. Which friend is right?
check.explanation: 3/5 off is 60% off. Percent means out of 100, so scale 3/5 to a denominator of 100: 5 × 20 = 100 and 3 × 20 = 60, giving 60/100 = 60%. Reading the digits 3 and 5 as '35%' ignores what the fraction means.
check.stemEs: «3/5 de descuento» significa que 3 de las 5 partes iguales se le quitan al precio. ¿Qué amigo tiene razón?
check.explanationEs: 3/5 de descuento es 60% de descuento. Porcentaje significa por cada 100, así que escala 3/5 a un denominador de 100: 5 × 20 = 100 y 3 × 20 = 60, dando 60/100 = 60%. Leer los dígitos 3 y 5 como «35%» ignora lo que significa la fracción.
choicesEs: El amigo que dijo 60% de descuento
El amigo que dijo 35% de descuento
Las dos son la misma cantidad

check.explanation: 3/5 = 60/100, and 60 hundredths is written 0.6. You can also divide: 3 ÷ 5 = 0.6.
check.explanationEs: 3/5 = 60/100, y 60 centésimas se escriben 0.6. También puedes dividir: 3 ÷ 5 = 0.6.

check.stem: The game costs $40 and 3/5 comes off. How much is taken off?
check.explanation: Split $40 into 5 equal parts of $8. Three of those parts come off: 3 × $8 = $24. That matches 60% of $40 = $24.
check.stemEs: El juego cuesta $40 y se le quitan 3/5. ¿Cuánto se le quita?
check.explanationEs: Reparte $40 en 5 partes iguales de $8. Tres de esas partes se le quitan: 3 × $8 = $24. Eso coincide con el 60% de $40 = $24.

check.stem: So what do you actually pay for the game?
check.explanation: You keep the other 2 of the 5 parts: 2 × $8 = $16. Check it: $40 − $24 = $16.
check.stemEs: Entonces, ¿cuánto pagas de verdad por el juego?
check.explanationEs: Te quedas con las otras 2 de las 5 partes: 2 × $8 = $16. Compruébalo: $40 − $24 = $16.

connect.modelAnswer: The friend who said 60% is correct. 3/5 = 60/100 = 0.6 = 60%, because 5 × 20 = 100 so 3 × 20 = 60. On a $40 game that is $24 off, so the sale price is $16. The friend who said 35% just read the digits 3 and 5 instead of building a fraction out of 100.
connect.promptEs: El amigo que dijo ___% tiene razón porque 3/5 = ___ = ___%. El precio de oferta es $___.
connect.scenarioEs: Una tienda tiene una liquidación: «¡Todo a 3/5 de descuento!» Tu amigo dice que eso significa 35% de descuento. Otro amigo dice que es 60% de descuento. El precio original de un juego es $40.
connect.promptQuestionEs: ¿Quién tiene razón, y cuánto costaría el juego en oferta?
connect.modelAnswerEs: El amigo que dijo 60% tiene razón. 3/5 = 60/100 = 0.6 = 60%, porque 5 × 20 = 100 así que 3 × 20 = 60. En un juego de $40 eso son $24 de descuento, así que el precio de oferta es $16. El amigo que dijo 35% solo leyó los dígitos 3 y 5 en vez de armar una fracción sobre 100.
